due_gate: before ep01 p7-prompt consumes style.json CR-012
summary: style.json CR-012 needs one named exception added: the Hatter's hat price ticket marked 10/6. Hand-off from the BIB-0029 arbitration; memory-bible does not edit style.json.
why_handed_off: style.json is 06-art/art-director's file and is frozen at H2 (v1.2.0, locked_h2, BIB-0028). memory-bible ruled the costume side of DEF-p4-costume-001-b and wrote the ruling into bible/costumes.json COS-015.lettering_ruling, but left style.json untouched.

findings.issue: CR-012 allows in-world lettering only for 'DRINK ME', the 'EAT ME' currants, the 'W. RABBIT' brass plate and the 'ORANGE MARMALADE' jar label. The Hatter's hat price ticket 'In this style 10/6' is a canon detail required by the Bible (bible/characters/index.json CHAR-hatter, bible/politics.json FAC-mad-tea-party) and carried in bible/costumes.json COS-015, but it is not on that closed list. Any machine or human check of CR-012 against COS-015 reads as a violation.
findings.ruling_already_made: BIB-0029 (memory-bible, 2026-09-23): KEEP the ticket. A canon detail is granted a named exception rather than being dropped from the costume.
findings.required_amendment: Add to CR-012's allowed list: "the Hatter's hat price ticket, marked 10/6". Period hand-lettering, small, on a paper ticket tucked in the hat band. The short price mark 10/6 is what must read; the full phrase 'In this style 10/6' is not required on screen. CR-012's other clauses are unchanged - in particular Art Nouveau sets still carry no poster lettering or decorative text panels, and there is still no other on-screen text, subtitle, caption, logo or watermark.
findings.downstream_if_applied: None. COS-015 already carries the ticket as its working value and is not stale; no image is affected (auto-reroll budget is 0 and no prop or costume image is regenerated by this).
findings.alternative_if_rejected: If art-director or the user would rather keep CR-012's list closed, the ticket must be dropped from bible/costumes.json COS-015 visual/visual_en/components instead - route that back to 00-orchestration/memory-bible as a controlled change, because it removes a canon detail and needs a user ruling.
findings.disposition: ACCEPTED as proposed. The exception is applied, not re-routed.

art_director_ruling.decision: ACCEPT the exception. The lettering stays in the film and CR-012 now names it.
art_director_ruling.reasoning: The ticket is not a style choice, it is canon (ch011-p37), and it is exactly the class of lettering CR-012 was written to permit: small, in-world, period hand-inked, physically motivated on a real object. CR-012 exists to keep Mucha poster lettering and any modern overlay out of frame, not to strip the Bible's own props and costume marks. A hand-inked price tag in a hat band is also period-true under CR-002 (1862 trade practice) and carries no Art Nouveau display typography, so admitting it costs the rule nothing. Rejecting it would have deleted a canon detail to protect a whitelist, which is the wrong way round.
art_director_ruling.redo_cost_assessment: Zero. No image is regenerated (user re-roll budget 0). COS-015 already carries the ticket as its working value, so no costume, prop or concept artefact becomes stale, and no p7 prompt that has already been written changes meaning. The five prompt-consumed fields (style_fragment_ui / style_fragment_en / style_string_en / negative_prompt_en / negative_prompt_waking_addon_en) are byte-identical, so nothing downstream must be re-emitted.
guardrails_attached: The ticket is the ONE named costume exception; no other garment, tabard, sash or accessory carries readable text (written into downstream_notes['character-concept / costume']).
Only the short price mark 10/6 need read on screen; the full phrase 'In this style 10/6' is not required.
The tag stays at real size, hand-inked, tucked in the hat band; never set as poster, display or decorative lettering.
Every other CR-012 clause is unchanged: Art Nouveau sets carry no poster lettering or decorative text panels, and there is no other on-screen text, subtitle, caption, logo or watermark.
